title: Bombay Aloo
subtitle: Spiced potatoes fried until golden and tender
excerpt: Waxy potatoes tossed in mustard seeds, turmeric, and ground spices then fried until the edges catch. A versatile side that pairs with flatbreads, rice, or grilled meat.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian spiced potato dish common across British-Indian restaurant cooking and home kitchens.

recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the batch and reheat in a dry pan to crisp the potatoes again.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Boil the potatoes up to a day ahead. Fry and spice just before serving.

content.text: Bombay aloo is a dry spiced potato dish with a slight crisp edge. The potatoes need to be fully cooked before they hit the frying pan. Do not rush the frying stage or the spices will not bloom properly.
Boil the potato chunks in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until just tender. Drain and leave to steam dry for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Wait until they pop, about 30 seconds.
Add the onion and fry for 8 minutes until golden at the edges. Stir regularly but not constantly.
Add the garlic and ginger. Fry for 2 minutes until fragrant. Do not let them scorch.
Add the turmeric, cumin, coriander, chilli powder, and salt. Stir for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
Add the drained potatoes. Fold them through the spice mixture. Press lightly with a spatula so they make contact with the pan base.
Fry for 8 minutes, turning every 2 minutes. You want some golden crust on the potato edges.
Remove from the heat. Sprinkle over the garam masala. Add lemon juice and fresh coriander if using. Serve straight away.

items.cause: They were overcooked during boiling or stirred too vigorously in the pan.
items.fix: Boil only until just tender. Turn carefully with a spatula rather than stirring.

items.symptom: The spices taste raw and harsh.
items.cause: They were added and the dish was served immediately without toasting them first.
items.fix: Give the dry spices at least 30 seconds in the hot fat before adding the potatoes.

items.symptom: The dish is dry and sticking badly.
items.cause: The pan was too hot or there was not enough oil.
items.fix: Add a splash of water and reduce the heat. The water will steam and loosen everything.
